1-1: A level crossing with a barrier is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. Outside built-up areas the sign is repeated at least 50 metres before the hazard.
1-2: A level crossing without a barrier is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. Outside built-up areas the sign is repeated at least 50 metres before the hazard.
1-3-1: A single-track level crossing without a barrier is ahead. The sign stands right before the crossing.
1-3-2: A level crossing without a barrier, with two or more tracks, is ahead. The sign stands right before the crossing.
1-4-1--1-4-6: Outside built-up areas these signs give an extra warning that you are approaching a level crossing. Signs 1.4.1–1.4.3 stand on the right side of the road, 1.4.4–1.4.6 on the left. Signs 1.4.1 and 1.4.4 stand with the first sign 1.1 or 1.2, 1.4.3 and 1.4.6 with the repeated sign 1.1 or 1.2, and 1.4.2 and 1.4.5 on their own, halfway between them.
1-5: A tram line crosses the road ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-6: An intersection of equal roads is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-7-1: An intersection with a minor road is ahead: drivers on that road must give way to you. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-7-2--1-7-7: A minor road joins your road ahead: drivers on it must give way to you. Signs 1.7.2, 1.7.4 and 1.7.6 show a junction on the right, 1.7.3, 1.7.5 and 1.7.7 on the left. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-8: A roundabout marked with sign 4.3 is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-9: An intersection, pedestrian crossing or road section with traffic lights is ahead. This sign is not used before level crossings. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-10: A drawbridge or a ferry crossing is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. Outside built-up areas the sign is repeated at least 50 metres before the hazard.
1-11: The road ahead runs along an embankment or the shore of a reservoir. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. Outside built-up areas the sign is repeated at least 50 metres before the hazard.
1-12-1: A dangerous bend to the right is ahead — sharp or with limited visibility. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-12-2: A dangerous bend to the left is ahead — sharp or with limited visibility. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-13-1: Several dangerous bends are ahead, the first one to the right. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-13-2: Several dangerous bends are ahead, the first one to the left. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-14: A steep descent is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. If a descent and a climb follow each other, signs 1.14 and 1.15 may stand right before them, without plate 8.1.1.
1-15: A steep climb is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. If a descent and a climb follow each other, signs 1.14 and 1.15 may stand right before them, without plate 8.1.1.
1-16: The road ahead is slippery: tyres grip the road poorly (the grip coefficient is below 0.4). In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-17: The road surface ahead is damaged: waves, potholes or an uneven joint at a bridge. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-18: An artificial bump, built to make traffic slow down, is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-19: On the road section ahead, gravel or crushed stone may fly out from under wheels. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-20: A dangerous roadside is ahead: its condition does not meet the standards. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-21-1: The carriageway narrows on both sides ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-21-2: The carriageway narrows on the right ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-21-3: The carriageway narrows on the left ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-22: Two-way traffic begins ahead, after a one-way section. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-23: A pedestrian crossing marked with signs 5.19.1 and 5.19.2 and/or markings 1.14.1–1.14.3 is ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. Outside built-up areas the sign is repeated at least 50 metres before the hazard.
1-24: A children's facility is nearby, so children may appear on the road. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. The sign is repeated both in and outside built-up areas, at least 50 metres before the hazard.
1-25: A cycle path marked with sign 4.4 crosses the road ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-26: Road works are going on ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it. The sign is repeated both in and outside built-up areas, at least 50 metres before the hazard. For short-term works the sign stands 10–15 metres before the work site, without plate 8.1.1.
1-27: The road ahead passes a farm or a livestock crossing, so animals may appear on the road. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-28: The road ahead passes a nature reserve, hunting ground or forest where wild animals may appear. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-29: The road section ahead is not protected from avalanches, landslides or falling rocks. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-30: A strong side wind may blow on the road section ahead. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-31: The road ahead passes close to an airfield, where planes or helicopters fly low. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-32: A tunnel is ahead that is not lit, or whose entrance, because of the terrain, can be seen from less than 150 metres. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-33: The road section ahead is temporarily blocked. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-34: Warns of a danger that no other warning sign covers. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the hazard, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
1-35-1--1-35-6: Shows which way a sharp bend with limited visibility turns: 1.35.1–1.35.3 to the right, 1.35.4–1.35.6 to the left. They also show the way around road works.
1-36-1--1-36-2: Shows the direction of travel at a T-junction or a fork in the road — to the right and to the left. It also shows the way around road works.
2-1: Main road: you have priority at unregulated intersections. The sign stands at the start of the road and is repeated before every intersection. With plate 8.13 it shows that the main road changes direction at the intersection: in a built-up area it stands before the intersection, outside one 150–300 metres before it and again before the intersection.
2-2: The main road ends here: from this point the road is no longer a main road. If the main road ends before an intersection, in a built-up area the sign stands 25 metres before the intersection and/or together with sign 2.3 or 2.4, outside one in advance, together with sign 2.4. The sign may also stand at the distance shown on plate 8.1.1.
2-3: Give way: at the intersection you must give way to traffic on the crossing road, or, with plate 8.13, to traffic on the main road. Outside built-up areas the sign also stands in advance, 150–300 metres before the intersection: with plate 8.1.1 if sign 2.3 stands before the intersection, or with plate 8.1.2 if sign 2.4 stands there. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before.
2-4: Driving on without stopping is banned: stop at the stop line, or, if there is none, at the edge of the carriageway you are crossing. Then give way to traffic on the crossing road, or, with plate 8.13, to traffic on the main road. The sign stands where the crossing road is hard to see, and may also stand at a level crossing or a quarantine post: then you stop at the stop line, or, if there is none, at the sign.
2-5: On the narrow section oncoming traffic has priority: you may not enter it if you would get in the way of oncoming traffic. Give way to an oncoming vehicle that is on the narrow section or at its far end. The sign stands right before the narrow section, or in advance with plate 8.1.1.
2-6: On the narrow section you have priority: oncoming vehicles must give way to you. The sign stands right before the narrow section.
3-1: No entry in this direction for all vehicles. The sign does not apply to route vehicles.
3-2: Traffic is banned for all vehicles, in both directions. The sign does not apply to route vehicles. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination. Nor does it apply to a vehicle driven by, or carrying, a person with a significant or severe disability.
3-3: All motor vehicles are banned, in both directions. The sign does not apply to route vehicles. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination. Nor does it apply to a vehicle driven by, or carrying, a person with a significant or severe disability.
3-4: A vehicle or combination whose maximum permitted mass is more than shown on the sign may not go on. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination.
3-5: Motorcycles of all kinds are banned. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination.
3-6: Tractors and self-propelled machines are banned. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination.
3-7: Lorries and tractors with a trailer are banned, and so is towing a motor vehicle. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination.
3-8: Horse-drawn vehicles, pack and riding animals are banned, and so is driving livestock. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign does not apply to vehicles serving a business in the zone, or serving or owned by people who live or work there: such vehicles enter and leave the zone at the intersection nearest to their destination.
3-9: Bicycles and mopeds are banned. Traffic is banned in both directions.
3-10: No pedestrians: the sign stands where walking is dangerous for them. It applies only to the side of the road where it stands.
3-11: A vehicle or combination whose actual total mass is more than shown on the sign may not go on.
3-12: A vehicle may not go on if the actual load on any of its axles is more than shown on the sign.
3-13: A vehicle may not go on if its height, with or without load, is more than shown on the sign.
3-14: A vehicle may not go on if its width, with or without load, is more than shown on the sign.
3-15: A vehicle or combination may not go on if its length, with or without load, is more than shown on the sign.
3-16: You may not drive closer to the vehicle in front than the distance shown on the sign. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it.
3-17-1: At a customs checkpoint on Georgia's customs border, driving on without stopping is banned.
3-17-2: Because of a road accident or another danger, all vehicles are banned from going further.
3-17-3: Driving past the checkpoint without stopping is banned: for example, a police or quarantine post, the entry to a border or closed zone, or the exit to a toll road.
3-18-1: Turning right at the nearest intersection is banned. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before. The sign does not apply to route vehicles.
3-18-2: Turning left at the nearest intersection is banned. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before. The sign does not apply to route vehicles.
3-19: U-turns at the nearest intersection are banned. The sign does not apply to route vehicles.
3-20: Overtaking any motor vehicle is banned, except one going slower than 30 km/h. You may overtake a motorcycle without a sidecar, a moped or a bicycle if you do not move into the oncoming lane. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it.
3-21: This is the end of sign 3.20 (“No overtaking”).
3-22: Lorries with a maximum permitted mass over 3.5 tonnes may not overtake, except vehicles going slower than 30 km/h. Tractors may not overtake either, except horse-drawn vehicles and bicycles. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it.
3-23: This is the end of sign 3.22 (“No overtaking for lorries”).
3-24: Driving faster than the speed on the sign (km/h) is banned. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it. If the sign stands before a built-up area, it applies up to sign 5.23.1 or 5.23.2 marking the built-up area.
3-25: This is the end of sign 3.24 (“Maximum speed limit”).
3-26: Sounding the horn is banned, except when you need it to prevent a road accident. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it.
3-27: Both stopping and parking are banned. The sign does not apply to route vehicles. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it. The sign applies only to the side of the road where it stands.
3-28: Parking is banned. The sign does not apply to a post vehicle (a white diagonal stripe on a blue background on its body) or to a taxi with its meter on. Nor does it apply to a vehicle driven by, or carrying, a person with a significant or severe disability. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. Exits from adjacent areas and junctions with field, forest or other minor roads do not end it. The sign applies only to the side of the road where it stands.
3-29: Parking is banned on odd days of the month. If signs 3.29 and 3.30 stand together, vehicles are moved from one side of the road to the other between 19:00 and 21:00, and during that time parking is allowed on both sides. Exceptions, reach and side are the same as for sign 3.28.
3-30: Parking is banned on even days of the month. If signs 3.29 and 3.30 stand together, vehicles are moved from one side of the road to the other between 19:00 and 21:00, and during that time parking is allowed on both sides. Exceptions, reach and side are the same as for sign 3.28.
3-31: Several signs end here at once: 3.16, 3.20, 3.22, 3.24, 3.26–3.30.
3-32: Vehicles carrying dangerous goods, which by law must have an identification sign, are banned. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign keeps such vehicles on their route and out of roads or areas where they would put people in special danger.
3-33: Vehicles carrying explosive and easily flammable goods (classes 1.22–2.4, 3.1, 3.2 and 5.2 of state standard 19433-88), which must have the “Dangerous goods” identification sign, are banned. Traffic is banned in both directions. The sign keeps such vehicles on their route and out of roads or areas where they would put people in special danger.
4-1-1: You may only go straight on. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before and does not apply to route vehicles. If the sign stands at the start of a road section, it applies up to the nearest intersection. It does not ban turning right into a yard or another adjacent area.
4-1-2: You may only turn right. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before and does not apply to route vehicles.
4-1-3: You may only turn left. U-turns are allowed too. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before and does not apply to route vehicles.
4-1-4: You may only go straight on or turn right. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before and does not apply to route vehicles.
4-1-5: You may only go straight on or turn left. U-turns are allowed too. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before and does not apply to route vehicles.
4-1-6: You may only turn right or left. U-turns are allowed too. The sign applies at the intersection it stands before and does not apply to route vehicles.
4-2-1: Pass the dividing strip, safety island or other obstacle only on the right.
4-2-2: Pass the dividing strip, safety island or other obstacle only on the left.
4-2-3: You may pass the dividing strip, safety island or other obstacle on either the right or the left.
4-3: There is a roundabout at the intersection: drive in the direction of the arrows.
4-4: Cycle path: a path for bicycles, built separately from the road and its other parts. The sign stands at the start of the path and is repeated after every crossing with a road.
4-5: Footpath: a path for pedestrians, separate from the road. The sign stands at the start of the path and is repeated after every crossing with a road.
4-6: You may not drive slower than the speed on the sign: it is the minimum speed. The sign applies from where it stands to the nearest intersection; in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area.
4-7: This is the end of sign 4.6 (“Minimum speed limit”).
4-9-1--4-9-3: Shows which way a vehicle carrying dangerous goods, which must have the “Dangerous goods” identification sign, may go.
4-8: On this section a vehicle must have snow chains on at least two driving wheels.
5-1: Motorway: motorway rules apply here. The sign stands at the start of the motorway, or near it with plate 8.1.1.
5-2: The motorway marked with sign 5.1 ends here. The sign stands at the end of the motorway, at its exits, and in advance with plate 8.1.1, 400 and 1000 metres before the end.
5-3: Road for motor vehicles: it is only for cars and motorcycles.
5-4: The road for motor vehicles marked with sign 5.3 ends here.
5-5: One-way road: across its whole width vehicles travel in one direction.
5-6: The one-way road or carriageway marked with sign 5.5 ends here.
5-7-1: Shows that you are entering a one-way road or carriageway. The sign stands before every side entry; it may be left out at an exit from an adjacent area if that area can only be entered from the road marked with sign 5.5.
5-7-2: Shows that you are entering a one-way road or carriageway. The sign stands before every side entry; it may be left out at an exit from an adjacent area if that area can only be entered from the road marked with sign 5.5.
5-8: A reversible traffic section begins: here the direction on one or more lanes may be switched to the opposite.
5-9: The reversible traffic section marked with sign 5.8 ends here.
5-10: Shows that you are entering a road with reversible traffic (the section marked with sign 5.8). The sign stands before every side entry; it may be left out at an exit from an adjacent area if that area can only be entered from the road marked with sign 5.8.
5-11: This road has a separate lane where route vehicles travel against the general flow. The sign applies to the lane it stands above.
5-12: The road with a route-vehicle lane marked with sign 5.11 ends here.
5-13-1: Shows that you are entering a road with a route-vehicle lane (the road marked with sign 5.11). The sign stands before every side entry; it may be left out at an exit from an adjacent area if that area can only be entered from the road marked with sign 5.11.
5-13-2: Shows that you are entering a road with a route-vehicle lane (the road marked with sign 5.11). The sign stands before every side entry; it may be left out at an exit from an adjacent area if that area can only be entered from the road marked with sign 5.11.
5-14: The lane is for route vehicles travelling here in the same direction as the general flow. The sign applies to the lane it stands above; a sign on the right side of the road applies to the rightmost lane.
5-15-1: Shows the number of lanes and which directions you may take from each lane. If the sign allows a turn from the leftmost lane, a U-turn from that lane is allowed too. A sign before an intersection applies to the whole intersection unless another sign 5.15.1 or 5.15.2 there says otherwise. The sign does not apply to route vehicles.
5-15-2: Shows which directions you may take from this lane. If the sign allows a turn from the leftmost lane, a U-turn from that lane is allowed too. A sign before an intersection applies to the whole intersection unless another sign 5.15.1 or 5.15.2 there says otherwise. The sign does not apply to route vehicles.
5-15-3: An extra lane on a climb, or a braking lane at a fork or junction, begins. If sign 4.6 (“Minimum speed limit”) is also shown on the sign, a driver who cannot keep the shown speed or more in the main lane must move to the extra lane.
5-15-4: On a three-lane road, a section of the middle lane meant for your direction begins.
5-15-5: The extra lane on a climb or the braking lane ends here.
5-15-6: On a three-lane road, the section of the middle lane meant for your direction ends.
5-15-7: Shows the number of lanes and the direction of traffic in each. If a lane shows a sign that bans some vehicle, that vehicle may not use the lane.
5-15-8: Shows how many lanes there are in your direction and which rule applies to each. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–150 metres before the start of the section, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
5-16: A bus and/or trolleybus stop, and also a taxi rank.
5-17: A tram stop, and also a taxi rank.
5-19-1: Pedestrian crossing. The sign stands on the right side of the road; if the crossing has no 1.14 marking, it stands at the near edge of the crossing.
5-19-2: Pedestrian crossing. The sign stands on the left side of the road; if the crossing has no 1.14 marking, it stands at the far edge of the crossing.
5-20: There is an artificial bump on the carriageway here. The sign stands right at the bump or at marking 1.25, on the side vehicles approach from.
5-21: A residential zone begins: residential zone rules apply here. The sign stands at every entry.
5-22: The residential zone marked with sign 5.21 ends here. The sign stands at every exit.
5-23-1: A built-up area begins, where built-up area traffic rules apply. The sign stands at every entry.
5-23-2: A built-up section begins that is not part of any built-up area (for example a holiday village or a stand-alone institution), but built-up area traffic rules apply here too. The sign stands at every entry.
5-24-1: The built-up area marked with sign 5.23.1 ends here. The sign stands at every exit, at the actual edge of the built-up area.
5-24-2: The built-up area marked with sign 5.23.2 ends here. The sign stands at every exit, at the actual edge of the built-up area.
5-25: A built-up area begins where built-up area traffic rules do not apply. The sign stands at every entry.
5-26: The built-up area marked with sign 5.25 ends here. The sign stands at every exit, at the actual edge of the built-up area.
5-27: A zone begins where parking is regulated or the maximum speed is limited, as shown on the sign. The sign stands at every entry.
5-28: The zone marked with sign 5.27 ends here. The sign stands at every exit.
5-29: A zone begins where parking is regulated or the maximum speed is limited, as shown on the sign. The sign stands at every entry.
5-30: The regulated parking zone marked with sign 5.29 ends here. The sign stands at every exit.
5-31: A zone begins where parking is regulated or the maximum speed is limited, as shown on the sign. The sign stands at every entry.
5-32: The maximum speed zone marked with sign 5.31 ends here. The sign stands at every exit.
5-33: A pedestrian zone begins: only pedestrians may move here. The sign stands at every entry.
5-34: The pedestrian zone marked with sign 5.33 ends here. The sign stands at every exit.
5-35: A medical facility is close to the road. When passing the sign, avoid unnecessary noise as far as you can.
5-36: Here the slip road (acceleration lane) from another road joins the motorway.
6-1: A first aid point is nearby.
6-3: A car service point is nearby.
6-6: A place to eat is nearby.
6-8: A hotel or motel is nearby.
6-11: A patrol police post is nearby.
6-13: An international road transport checkpoint is nearby.
6-14: In this zone you can hear a radio station that broadcasts road traffic information.
6-15: In this zone you can reach the emergency services by radio.
6-16: A swimming pool or beach is nearby.
7-1: Tells you the general speed limits that apply on Georgian roads under the traffic rules. The sign stands at the entry to Georgia, at a border checkpoint.
7-2: Recommends the speed to drive at on this section. The sign stands at the start of the road and applies up to the nearest intersection; with a warning sign, along the whole dangerous section.
7-3-1: This is a U-turn place. The sign stands before or at the turning place, or in advance with plate 8.1.1. It does not allow a left turn.
7-3-2: Shows the length of the U-turn zone. The sign stands before or at the turning place, or in advance with plate 8.1.1. It does not allow a left turn.
7-4: Parking place. Road markings define the zone; without markings the sign applies up to the nearest intersection, or as limited by plate 8.2.1.
7-5: An emergency stopping lane on a steep descent. The sign stands before the entry to the lane.
7-6: An underground pedestrian crossing. The sign stands at every way down to it.
7-7: An overhead pedestrian crossing. The sign stands at every way up to it.
7-8-1: Dead end: this road has no through exit. The sign stands at the start of such a road.
7-8-2: Dead end: this road has no through exit. The sign stands before the junction with the road that leads into the dead end.
7-8-3: Dead end: this road has no through exit. The sign stands before the junction with the road that leads into the dead end.
7-9-3: Shows the traffic layout at an intersection where some manoeuvres are banned, or the allowed directions at a complex intersection. The sign stands right before the intersection.
7-9-1: Shows the way to a built-up area or another place, and the way around a section with restrictions. The bottom of the sign shows the distance to the intersection or to the start of the braking lane. Outside built-up areas, a green background means you reach the place by motorway, blue — by another road. In a built-up area, a green or blue background means that after leaving it you go by motorway or by another road, and a white background means the place is in this same built-up area.
7-9-2: Shows the way to a built-up area or another place, and the way around a section with restrictions. Outside built-up areas, a green background means you reach the place by motorway, blue — by another road. In a built-up area, a green or blue background means that after leaving it you go by motorway or by another road, and a white background means the place is in this same built-up area.
7-10-2: Shows the direction to a built-up area or another place and the distance to it (km). Outside built-up areas, a green background means you reach the place by motorway, blue — by another road. In a built-up area, a green or blue background means that after leaving it you go by motorway or by another road, and a white background means the place is in this same built-up area.
7-10-1: Shows the directions to built-up areas or other places and the distances to them (km). Outside built-up areas, a green background means you reach the place by motorway, blue — by another road. In a built-up area, a green or blue background means that after leaving it you go by motorway or by another road, and a white background means the place is in this same built-up area.
7-12: Shows the distances (km) to built-up areas or other places on the route.
7-11: Shows the name of a place that is not a built-up area: a street, river, lake, mountain pass, landmark and so on. The sign stands right before the place.
7-13: Shows the distance (km) to the start or end of the road. The sign stands every kilometre.
7-14-2: Shows the road (route) number and direction.
7-15-1--7-15-3: If lorries, tractors or self-propelled machines are banned in some direction at an intersection, this sign shows the recommended way for them. It stands before the intersection or 100–150 metres before it.
7-16: Stop line: shows where to stop at a regulated intersection or an unregulated level crossing.
7-18-1--7-18-3: Shows which way to go around a temporarily closed section. The signs stand before every intersection on the detour route.
7-17: Shows how to go around a temporarily closed section. In a built-up area the sign stands 50–100 metres before the intersection where the detour starts, outside one 150–300 metres before it.
7-19-1: Shows how to get around a closed section on a road with a dividing strip by moving to the other carriageway, or how to return to the right-hand carriageway.
7-19-2: Shows how to get around a closed section on a road with a dividing strip by moving to the other carriageway, or how to return to the right-hand carriageway.
8-1-1--8-1-4: The plate shows the distance from the sign to the hazard, to where a restriction begins, or to a place ahead. 8.1.2 shows the distance from sign 2.3 to the intersection when sign 2.4 stands before the intersection. 8.1.3 and 8.1.4 show the distance to a place off to the side of the road.
8-2-1--8-2-6: The plate shows the length of the dangerous section with a warning sign, or the zone of a prohibitory or information sign. 8.2.3 shows the end of the zone of signs 3.27–3.30, and 8.2.4 tells you that you are still in their zone. 8.2.5 and 8.2.6 show the zone of signs 3.27–3.30 along one side of a square, building front and so on.
8-3-1--8-3-3: The plate shows which way a sign before an intersection applies, or which way a place near the road lies.
8-4-1: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to: lorries (with or without a trailer) with a maximum permitted mass over 3.5 tonnes.
8-4-2: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to: lorries or tractors with any trailer or semi-trailer, and vehicles towing a motor vehicle.
8-4-3: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to: cars.
8-4-4: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to — the one shown on the plate.
8-4-5: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to — the one shown on the plate.
8-4-6: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to — the one shown on the plate.
8-4-7: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to — the one shown on the plate.
8-4-8: The plate shows which type of vehicle the sign applies to: vehicles with the “Dangerous goods” identification sign.
8-5-1: The plate shows that the sign applies on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
8-5-2: The plate shows that the sign applies on working days.
8-5-3: The plate shows the days of the week when the sign applies.
8-5-4: The plate shows the time of day when the sign applies.
8-5-5: The plate shows the days of the week and the time of day when the sign applies.
8-5-6: The plate shows the days of the week and the time of day when the sign applies.
8-5-7: The plate shows the days of the week and the time of day when the sign applies.
8-6-1: The plate shows how to park vehicles in the parking area: all of them on the carriageway, along the pavement.
8-6-2: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-3: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-4: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-5: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-6: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-7: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-8: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-6-9: The plate shows how to park a car or motorcycle in a parking area next to the pavement, as drawn on the plate.
8-7: In the parking area marked with sign 7.4 you may only park with the engine off.
8-8: Parking in the area marked with sign 7.4 is paid.
8-9: Parking time in the area marked with sign 7.4 is limited.
8-10: In the area marked with sign 7.4 or 6.10 there is an inspection ramp or pit for cars.
8-11: The sign applies only to vehicles whose maximum permitted mass is more than shown on the plate.
8-12: Moving onto the roadside is dangerous because repair work is going on there. The plate is used with sign 1.26.
8-13: The plate shows which way the main road goes at the intersection. It stands with signs 2.1, 2.3 and 2.4 when the main road changes direction at the intersection.
8-14: The plate shows the lane a sign or traffic light applies to. It stands above the lane.
8-15: Blind or visually impaired people use this pedestrian crossing. The plate is used with signs 1.23, 5.19.1 and 5.19.2 and with traffic lights.
8-16: The sign applies only when the road surface is wet. The plate is used with signs 1.16, 3.20, 3.22 and 3.24.
8-17: The parking area marked with sign 7.4 is only for vehicles with the “Person with disabilities” identification sign.
8-18: The sign does not apply to vehicles with the “Person with disabilities” identification sign.
8-19: The sign applies to vehicles carrying dangerous goods of the class shown on the plate (under state standard 19433-88). The plate is used with signs 3.32, 3.33 and 4.9.1–4.9.3.
8-20-1--8-20-2: The plate shows how many closely spaced axles a vehicle has; each of them may carry the mass shown on sign 3.12.
8-21-1: The plate marks a parking area at a metro station. It is used with sign 7.4.
8-21-2: The plate marks a bus and/or trolleybus parking area at a metro station. It is used with sign 7.4.
8-21-3: The plate marks a tram parking area at a metro station. It is used with sign 7.4.
8-22-1--8-22-3: The plate is used with signs 4.2.1, 4.2.2 and 4.2.3 to help you find your way around an obstacle.
marking-1-1: Solid line: separates opposite traffic flows and marks lane edges in dangerous places; it also marks carriageway edges where entry is banned, the edges of parking places, and the edges of the carriageway (except on motorways). Crossing line 1.1 is banned. Exception: you may cross a 1.1 line on your right that marks the edge of the carriageway to stop on the roadside.
marking-1-2: Wide solid line: marks the edge of the carriageway on a motorway. You may cross it to stop on the roadside.
marking-1-3: Double solid line: separates opposite traffic flows on a road with four or more lanes. Crossing line 1.3 is banned.
marking-1-4: Marks a place where stopping is banned. It is used on its own or with sign 3.27, along the edge of the carriageway or on top of the kerb.
marking-1-5: Broken line: separates opposite traffic flows on a two- or three-lane road, and marks lane edges when there are two or more lanes in one direction. You may cross it from either side.
marking-1-6: Approach line: a broken line whose dashes are three times longer than the gaps. It warns that you are approaching marking 1.1 or 1.11 that separates traffic flows. You may cross it from either side.
marking-1-7: Broken line with short dashes and equal gaps: marks traffic lanes within an intersection. You may cross it from either side.
marking-1-8: Wide broken line: marks the border between an acceleration or braking lane and the main lane (at intersections, at grade-separated junctions, at bus stops and so on). You may cross it from either side.
marking-1-9: Marks the edges of reversible lanes. When the reversible traffic lights are off, it separates opposite traffic flows.
marking-1-10: Marks a place where parking is banned. It is used on its own or with sign 3.28, along the edge of the carriageway or on top of the kerb.
marking-1-11: A solid and a broken line together: separates flows where changing lanes is allowed from one side only, or marks turning places and entries to and exits from parking areas. You may cross it from the broken-line side; from the solid-line side, only to finish overtaking or passing an obstacle.
marking-1-12: Stop line: shows where to stop when sign 2.4 stands there, or at a red traffic light or a traffic controller's stop signal.
marking-1-13: Shows where to stop, if needed, to give way to traffic on the crossing road.
marking-1-14-2: “Zebra”: marks an unregulated pedestrian crossing. The arrows show the direction pedestrians walk.
marking-1-14-3: Marks a pedestrian crossing controlled by traffic lights.
marking-1-15: Marks the place where a cycle path crosses the carriageway.
marking-1-16-1--1-16-3: Marks guiding islands where traffic flows split or merge.
marking-1-17: Marks route vehicle stops and taxi ranks.
marking-1-18: Lane arrows: show which directions you may take at the intersection from this lane. Used on their own or with signs 5.15.1 and 5.15.2. A dead-end symbol means turning onto the nearest carriageway is banned; if you may turn left from the leftmost lane, you may also make a U-turn from it.
marking-1-19: Warns that the carriageway narrows ahead (fewer lanes in your direction), or that you are approaching marking 1.1 or 1.11 separating opposite flows. When the road narrows, it may be used with signs 1.21.1–1.21.3.
marking-1-20: Warns that you are approaching marking 1.13.
marking-1-21: The word “STOP”: warns that you are approaching marking 1.12 when it is used with sign 2.4.
marking-1-23: Marks a lane meant for route vehicles.
